title: The Tunnel Exposed
narrative: Holmes reconstructs the scheme: Clay used the Red-Headed League to lock Wilson in the office while he dug beneath the pawnshop. Jones confirms the scar and the prison record. Clay is arrested before reaching the vault, Ross is taken in as an accomplice, and Wilson recovers his dignity by admitting how the trick worked.
truth_reveal: The League was a deliberate distraction.
Clay dug the tunnel toward the bank.
Ross recruited Wilson and helped run the false office.

character_fates.ross: Held as an accomplice who cooperates with the investigation.
character_fates.wilson: Keeps the pawnshop and tells the story honestly.
character_fates.holmes: Solves the case through the evidence chain.
character_fates.watson: Records the human details behind the deception.
character_fates.jones: Makes the arrest with physical proof.

title: The Wrong Middleman
narrative: Ross is exposed as the organizer in the room, but the tunnel evidence points beyond him. Clay escapes into the night before the police can close the streets. The group discovers the truth too late: the visible conspirator was not the architect.
truth_reveal: Clay designed the tunnel and used an alias.
The evidence was divided between the office and the basement.

character_fates.wilson: Learns that embarrassment delayed the investigation.
character_fates.holmes: Regrets not securing the arrest sooner.

title: A Case Left Open
narrative: The group refuses to accuse anyone. Holmes can explain the tunnel, but without a named suspect the law moves slowly. By morning the evidence is clear, yet Clay has already disappeared.
truth_reveal: A tunnel was dug toward the bank.
The League was a planned distraction.
The strongest evidence points to Clay.

character_fates.ross: Is questioned but not charged immediately.
character_fates.wilson: Closes the League office for good.
character_fates.watson: Publishes a warning about easy money.
